column1: # Test run policy table (issue #407 item 3) — single source of truth for
# per-class QEMU run policy. Consumed ONLY via tools/test-policy.awk
# anywhere else. `|` separator survives editors/formatters (no TABs).
# Tiers, lowest precedence first (later line wins within a tier):
# An arch record beats a group record (riscv64 always 400 s, even heavy).
# `members` rows are resolver metadata (group membership), not policy.
# Each row carries its originating issue as provenance.
# Reserved: `requires|ovmf` key for q35 OVMF guards (deferred follow-up).
group|heavy|members|core_basic core_sync core_sched core_task core_memory core_syscall core_tracing smp_multicpu ahci_live iommu_live deadline
# Rule: expect_timeout = ceil(measured normal-pass wall x 1.3), per arch,
# via arch-qualified class selectors (arch:class beats bare class).
# Baselines below measured 2026-10-25 on a LOADED host (load 5-12 x86_64,
# 3-6 aarch64) — upper bounds, strictly tighter than the 120/250 defaults
# they replace. Refresh from unloaded/CI runs when available; a TCG trip
# of a 30pct margin is a flake (root-cause/file), never a silent inflate.
# Classes with NO passing baseline keep the tier defaults (no row):
# list_tests.py AARCH64_CLASSES comment; issues #417/#418 where kernel-side).
# Outer wrapper untouched (600/1200 backstop, covers 2 attempts + compile).
# 1204ms; hal/bench/ahci times include one stall-retry cycle, conservative).
